body: Copper Giant Intersects 584 Metres of 0.73% CuEq* (0.40% Cu and 0.062% Mo), Exceeding the Mocoa Resource Model Ahead of the Anticipated PEA News provided by COPPER GIANT RESOURCES CORP. Jul 28, 2026, 07:30 ET Share this article Share to X Share this article Share to X VANCOUVER, BC, July 28, 2026 /CNW/ -- Copper Giant Resources Corp. ( "Copper Giant" or the "Company" ) (TSXV: CGNT ) (OTCQB: LBCMF) (FRA: 29H0) today reports assay results from infill hole MD-066 and corridor hole MD-065 at its flagship Mocoa copper-molybdenum porphyry project in Putumayo, Colombia. MD-066 intersected 584 metres of continuous mineralization grading 0.73% CuEq* (0.40% Cu and 0.062% Mo), including a higher-grade core of 183 metres of 0.94% CuEq* (0.54% Cu and 0.076% Mo), well above the current MRE¹ average of 0.51% CuEq* (0.31% Cu and 0.039% Mo), confirming and locally exceeding the resource model that is used for the anticipated upcoming Preliminary Economic Assessment (" PEA "). MD-065, the first hole collared at the La Estrella target and the first assay result from the Company's third drill rig, reached the southeastern margin of the Mocoa system, returning 176 metres of 0.30% CuEq* (0.15% Cu and 0.027% Mo) from 610 metres, outside the current resource footprint. Grade increased continuously with depth and the hole ended in mineralization with the final 49 metres averaging 0.34% CuEq* (0.10% Cu and 0.046% Mo), open toward the higher-grade core to the northwest. Together these holes document a model reproducing grade and continuity at infill spacing, and mineralization beyond the MRE footprint. Drilling continues at La Estrella, with assays pending. Cross-section along MD-066 illustrating the geometry of infill drilling and intercepted Cu and Mo grades. The long mineralized intervals continue to confirm the scale and grade continuity of the deposit and provide increased geological confidence ahead of future PEA-level studies. Figure 2. Representative core photographs from holes MD-065 (A - C) and MD-066 (D - F) illustrating porphyry-style mineralization, hydrothermal alteration, and vein-hosted copper and molybdenum mineralization. Figure 3. Cross-section along hole MD-065 (section width of 100 metres), showing the 2026 MRE block model and the Cu and Mo grades intercepted. MD-065 was drilled from the La Estrella target into the southeastern margin of the Mocoa system, with mineralization strengthening at depth and remaining open toward the higher-grade core, supporting the interpreted continuity of the Mocoa – La Estrella corridor. Kick-off (KO) points for directional daughter holes are indicated. Figure 4. Plan view of holes MD-065 and MD-066 and the location of the cross-sections shown in Figures 1 and 3. MD-066 validates higher-grade domains within the MRE¹ footprint, while hole MD-065 links mineralization from the La Estrella target northwestward to the southeastern edge of Mocoa. Kick-off (KO) points for directional daughter holes are shown, illustrating the use of a single drill platform to test multiple targets. Figure 5. Plan view of the Mocoa porphyry Cu-Mo deposit and surrounding exploration targets. Black dots represent drill pads.
